mina: Heads up — seeing premature termination on streaming outputs for a chat template when the stop sequence is a multi-token EOS variant. Repro is flaky but consistent on one model (rwz-chat-1) after quantized bring-up. Anyone seen this?

raj: Can you paste the exact template + stop config and which tokenizer you used? also which conversion path from HF?

mina: Template: 'User: {user}
Assistant:' and we set stops = ['']. Tokenizer used is HF bpe converted by our hf->redwood script. Model's config.json had 'eos_token' set to ''. We ran int8 quantization in the onboarding PR and the behavior appeared after deploy.

sasha: Quick theory — our streaming runtime matches on decoded string prefixes and truncates as soon as the EOS string is emitted. If the HF tokenizer sometimes emits two tokens that together form the string (eg two consecutive '' tokens due to byte-level splitting), the runtime may stop early on the first token match but leave the second token in the KV cache, causing weird empty chunks downstream.

mina: I also repro'd locally: with stops=['

'] it's fine; with stops=[''] it cuts immediately and sometimes outputs an empty final chunk. Non-quantized baseline doesn't show the bug.

lorenzo: Did you try supplying stop_token_ids instead of string stops? if runtime matches by token id we avoid string split ambiguity.

mina: Tried stop_token_ids=[50256] — streaming still cut early on the quantized build. So it seems the int8 decoder path is doing a fuzzy prefix match on bytes.

raj: Ok please add a minimal repro (model + prompt) and tokenizer dumps. Also check if template has hidden chars (zero-width space) that change alignment — we've burned that before.

sasha: I'll run tokenizer diffs (HF python tokenizer vs our C++ runtime) across float32 vs int8 variants. If tokenization differs, we need to fix the hf->redwood converter to preserve special token normalization.

ci-bot: job #ci-eval-472 queued: eng-ml/stop-seq-repro. Link: https://ci.internal/ci-eval-472

mina: Filed INF-2143 with logs, minimal repro, and a short recording of streaming chunks. Workaround for now: avoid using '' as a stop string — prefer '

' or stop_token_ids where we control IDs, or insert a single space before the assistant marker to shift tokenization.

raj: Also add a regression test in onboarding that runs the streaming client against the quantized serving path with a few stop variants.

sasha: Agreed — i'll take tokenizer diff + a small unit that asserts streaming doesn't produce an empty final chunk. mina/lorenzo can own the INF ticket.

mina: Thanks all :thumbsup:
